:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem: Find the equation of the line that is perpendicular to $y = 4x - 1$ and passes through the point $(-8,7).$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Let $l_1$ denote the line $y = 4x - 1,$ and let $l_2$ denote the line we want to find.

Since perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other, the slope of $l_2$ is the negative reciprocal of the slope of $l_1.$ Since $l_1$ has a slope of $4,$ the line $l_2$ must have a slope of $-\dfrac{1}{4}.$

Our perpendicular line must have the slope $m=-\dfrac{1}{4}$ and pass through the point $(x_1,y_1)=(-8,7).$ Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the line:

$$
\eqalign{
y - y_1 &= m(x-x_1) \[5pt]
y - 7 &= -\dfrac{1}{4}(x-(-8)) \[5pt]
y - 7 &= -\dfrac{1}{4}(x+8)\[5pt]
y - 7 &= -\dfrac{1}{4}x - 2 \[5pt]
y &= -\dfrac{1}{4}x + 5
	}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let ${l}_{1}$ denote the line $y=4x-6,$ and let ${l}_{2}$ denote the line we want to find.

Since perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other, the slope of ${l}_{2}$ is the negative reciprocal of the slope of ${l}_{1}.$ Since ${l}_{1}$ has a slope of $4,$ the line ${l}_{2}$ must have a slope of $-\frac{1}{4}.$

Our perpendicular line must have the slope $m=-\frac{1}{4}$ and pass through the point $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(8,-3).$ Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the line in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-3) & =-\frac{1}{4}(x-8) \\ y+3 & =-\frac{1}{4}x+2 \\ y & =-\frac{1}{4}x-1\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: The lines $y=\frac{1}{2}x-3$ and $y=mx+b$ are perpendicular. Given that the line $y=mx+b$ passes through the point $(-1,5),$ what is the value of $b?$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let ${l}_{1}$ denote the line $y=\frac{1}{2}x-3,$ and let ${l}_{2}$ denote the line we want to find.

Since perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other, the slope of ${l}_{2}$ is the negative reciprocal of the slope of ${l}_{1}.$ Since ${l}_{1}$ has a slope of $\frac{1}{2},$ the line ${l}_{2}$ must have a slope of $-2.$

Our perpendicular line must have the slope $m=-2$ and pass through the point $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(-1,5).$ Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the line in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-5 & =-2(x-(-1)) \\ y-5 & =-2(x+1) \\ y-5 & =-2x-2 \\ y & =-2x+3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $b=3.$
